plan.title: Add kanban-quick command for fast implementation workflow
plan.overview: Create a streamlined /kanban-quick skill that combines task creation, scoping, planning, and implementation into a single workflow for small fixes and simple features. Uses minimal Q&A (problem + done), optional codebase research, creates a quick/{id} branch, stores a combined quick.xml artifact, and provides optional review pause before commit with optional doc updates. This provides a fast-track alternative to the full 8-column workflow while preserving git hygiene.

approach.rationale:
Following existing skill patterns: - Skill file structure: Handlebars partials for reusable components (kanban-create/SKILL.md) - Helper script pattern: Tagged union JSON errors (find-task.cjs, next-id.cjs) - AskUserQuestion usage: Structured questions (kanban-create/SKILL.md:66-77) - Directive compliance: Load via get-skill-config.cjs (directive-compliance partial)
Key design decisions: - Separate ID namespace (next-quick-id.cjs starts at 000) to avoid collision with task IDs - Separate storage (.kanban/quick/{id}/) to keep quick tasks isolated from full workflow - Must run on main branch (like kanban-create) since quick tasks don't use the full branch workflow - Self-contained: no PR flow, no integration with kanban-check/kanban-merge - Commit format: quick({id}): {title} per workflow.yaml pattern extension

task.name: Create next-quick-id.cjs helper script
task.action:
- Create script that scans .kanban/quick/ directory for existing quick task folders - Return JSON with nextId, currentHighest, padding (default 3) - Use separate sequence starting at 000 (not shared with task IDs) - Follow tagged union error pattern: {error: true, message} on failure - Return {nextId: "000", currentHighest: null, padding: 3} if no quick tasks exist
Reference implementation (next-id.cjs): ```javascript const TASKS_DIR = ".kanban/tasks"; // ...scans folders, finds highest numeric ID, returns nextId ```
Change to scan .kanban/quick/ instead: ```javascript const QUICK_DIR = ".kanban/quick"; // Same logic but for quick tasks ```
task.done: Script returns valid JSON with nextId field

task.name: Create find-quick.cjs helper script
task.done: Script returns error JSON (expected - no quick tasks yet) or valid JSON if quick exists

task.name: Create quick.xml template
task.action:
- Create XML template with combined task+spec+plan info - Include: id, created, updated attributes - Include: title, problem, done elements - Include: files element for identified/modified files - Include: commit element for hash, message, date - Include: docs element for optional doc updates
Template content: ```xml <quick id="{id}" created="{created}" updated="{updated}"> <title>{title}</title>
<problem>{what problem are you solving}</problem> <done>{what does done look like}</done>
<files> <file path="{path}" action="found|modified|created"/> </files>
<commit hash="{hash}" message="{message}" date="{date}"/>
<docs> <doc id="{id}" type="product|engineering"/> </docs> </quick> ```
task.done: Template file exists with valid XML structure

task.name: Create kanban-quick skill file
task.action:
- Create skill folder: apps/kanban/src/content/skills/kanban-quick/ - Create SKILL.md with frontmatter (name, description, allowed-tools, argument-hint, disable-model-invocation) - Use Handlebars partials: directory-reference, product-docs-scripts, engineering-docs-scripts
Process steps to implement: 1. load_workflow: Use workflow-load partial 2. verify_branch: Must be on main/master (use branch-verify-main pattern) 3. load_directives: Use load-directives partial for kanban-quick 4. get_next_quick_id: Run node .kanban/scripts/next-quick-id.cjs 5. get_title: From $ARGUMENTS or ask user 6. ask_problem (FR1): AskUserQuestion "What problem are you solving?" 7. ask_done (FR2): AskUserQuestion "What does done look like?" 8. (FR3 implicitly satisfied by NOT asking about value) 9. ask_research (FR4): AskUserQuestion "Want me to research the codebase first?" 10. optional_research (FR5): If yes, use Glob/Grep to find affected files 11. create_branch (FR6): git checkout -b quick/{id} 12. create_quick_xml (FR7): Create .kanban/quick/{id}/quick.xml 13. implement: Make the code changes 14. pause_for_review (FR8, FR9, FR10): Output message, ask ready to commit 15. directive_compliance (FR11): Use directive-compliance partial 16. commit (FR12): git commit -m "quick({id}): {title}" 17. update_quick_xml (FR16): Add commit hash, files modified 18. ask_docs (FR13): AskUserQuestion "Do you want me to update docs?" 19. detect_docs (FR14): If yes, scan changes for affected docs 20. update_docs: Update detected product/engineering docs 21. output_result: Summary + [KANBAN_COMPLETE]
Frontmatter: ```yaml --- name: kanban-quick description: Fast implementation for simple fixes, config changes, and small features. Minimal Q&A, optional research, single commit. allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash(node *, git add *, git commit *, git status, git branch *, git checkout *, git diff *), Grep, Glob, AskUserQuestion argument-hint: "[task description]" disable-model-invocation: true --- ```
task.done: Skill file exists and builds without errors

task.name: Add source files for new scripts
task.pattern: Script source pattern at apps/kanban/src/scripts/next-id.ts, apps/kanban/src/scripts/find-task.ts
task.action:
- The .kanban/scripts/*.cjs files are built outputs - Create TypeScript source files in apps/kanban/src/scripts/ - next-quick-id.ts: TypeScript source for the quick ID generator - find-quick.ts: TypeScript source for finding quick tasks - These will compile to .kanban/scripts/*.cjs via build process
Pattern from apps/kanban/src/scripts/next-id.ts: ```typescript const TASKS_DIR = ".kanban/tasks"; // ...logic ```
Create apps/kanban/src/scripts/next-quick-id.ts: ```typescript const QUICK_DIR = ".kanban/quick"; // ...same pattern but for quick tasks ```
task.done: TypeScript files compile and produce working .cjs outputs

Add after tasks line: ```markdown - **`.kanban/quick/{id}/`** — Quick task folder containing `quick.xml` (for /kanban-quick) ```
